records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהַעֲל֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ אֵלִיָּ֛הוּ וֶאֱלִישָׁ֖ע מִן־הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃
records.gloss: And it was, when took up Yahweh Elijah in the whirlwind [to] the heavens, and went Elijah and Elisha from the Gilgal.
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was about to take Elijah up to heaven by a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were setting out from Gilgal.

L.1: And it came about, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was taking Elijah up in the whirlwind [to] the heavens, that Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was about to take Elijah up into heaven in a whirlwind. At that time Elijah and Elisha were leaving the town of Gilgal.

decisions.choice: when Yahweh was taking Elijah up: the opening tells the reader what is about to happen
decisions.reason: The first words name the end of the story before it starts: the day Yahweh took Elijah up. Elijah himself (verses 9-10), Elisha and the company of prophets (verses 3, 5) all know it is coming. The verb form says when the journey happened, not that Elijah was already rising.

decisions.choice: the whirlwind: a violent storm wind sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word names a storm or gale, the kind of wind in which Yahweh appears and speaks (Job 38:1; Ezekiel 1:4). It is called "the" whirlwind because the story goes on to tell of it (verse 11). Elijah is carried up by the wind; the chariot of fire separates the two men (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Gilgal: probably a town in the hill country, not the camp by the Jordan
decisions.reason: From this Gilgal the two men "went down" to Bethel (verse 2), so it lay higher than Bethel, in the hills. The Gilgal where Israel camped after crossing the Jordan (Joshua 4:19) lay low near Jericho, which they reach only later (verse 4). The exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: were setting out / were leaving
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the journey was starting, since verse 1 sets the scene for the walk that follows.

decisions.choice: the town of Gilgal
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so the reader knows this is a place name.

records.heading: Elijah is taken up to heaven

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֜ע שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי עַד־בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּרְד֖וּ בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah to Elisha, Stay please here, for Yahweh has sent me as far as Bethel; and said Elisha, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I will leave you; and they went down [to] Bethel.
pieces: Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me on to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." Then they went down together to Bethel.

L.2: And Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, please, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me as far as Bethel." And Elisha said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." And they went down [to] Bethel.

R.2: Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to Bethel." But Elisha answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went down to Bethel.

decisions.choice: stay here, please: a request, perhaps also a test
decisions.reason: Elijah asks three times (verses 2, 4, 6) and Elisha refuses three times. The story does not say why Elijah asks: to spare Elisha, to go alone, or to see whether Elisha will hold on to him. Elisha's refusals show his loyalty to the end (compare Ruth 1:15-18).

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives: a double oath
decisions.reason: Swearing by the life of Yahweh is the strongest oath; Elisha adds the life of Elijah himself, as Jonathan and Abigail did with David (1 Samuel 20:3; 25:26). "Your soul" means simply "you" in person.

decisions.choice: if I leave you: means "I will not leave you"
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if I do this" leaves an unspoken curse on the speaker, so it means "I will certainly not do this" (1 Kings 17:1).

decisions.choice: Bethel: an old place of worship, and a center of the calf worship of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Bethel was where Jacob met God (Genesis 28:19). Jeroboam set up one of his golden calves there (1 Kings 12:28-29), and yet a company of prophets loyal to Yahweh lived there (verse 3).

decisions.choice: [as] your soul lives / as surely as you live
decisions.reason: The oath is worded as in 1 Samuel 20:3 and 25:26. Literal keeps "your soul"; Balanced and Readable say "you", which is what it means (m2). Literal says "I will not leave you" for the oath form (m3).

records.source: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בֵּֽית־אֵל֮ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הֲיָדַ֕עְתָּ כִּ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם יְהוָ֛ה לֹקֵ֥חַ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ מֵעַ֣ל רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם־אֲנִ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי הֶחֱשֽׁוּ׃
records.gloss: And came out [the] sons of the prophets who [were at] Bethel to Elisha and said to him, Do you know that today Yahweh [is] taking your master from over your head? And he said, Also I know; be silent.
pieces: The company of prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master from you today?" He said, "Yes, I know. Say no more."

L.3: And the sons of the prophets who [were at] Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know [it]; be silent."

R.3: A group of prophets lived at Bethel. They came out to meet Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master away from you today?" "Yes, I know," Elisha said. "Do not talk about it."

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets: members of a company of prophets
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means members of a group, not children. These were bands of prophets who lived and worked together, apparently under a leader they called "father" (verse 12; 6:1-2; 1 Kings 20:35). Elijah seems to have led them, and Elisha takes his place (verse 15).

decisions.choice: from over your head: away from you, as the one who stands over you
decisions.reason: Elijah is Elisha's master, the one above him. To take him "from over your head" is to remove him from his place as Elisha's leader. It may also hint at Elijah being taken up.

decisions.choice: I also know; be silent: Elisha already knows and does not want it spoken of
decisions.reason: Elisha knows as well as they do. His command to be quiet shows grief or that the matter is not for talk; he says no more and stays with his master.

decisions.choice: company of prophets
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sons of the prophets"; Balanced says "company of prophets" and Readable "group of prophets", as m1 explains.

decisions.choice: Say no more / Do not talk about it
decisions.reason: The command "be silent" means "do not speak of it", not that they had been shouting.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע׀שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי יְרִיח֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said to him Elijah, Elisha, stay please here, for Yahweh has sent me [to] Jericho; and he said, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I will leave you; and they came [to] Jericho.
pieces: Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.

L.4: And Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, please, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me [to] Jericho." And he said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." And they came [to] Jericho.

R.4: Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to Jericho." But Elisha answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So they went on to Jericho.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives, if I leave you: a firm oath that he will not leave
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: Jericho: the city near the Jordan, rebuilt in Ahab's time
decisions.reason: Joshua had laid a curse on anyone who rebuilt Jericho (Joshua 6:26), and it fell on Hiel of Bethel in Ahab's days (1 Kings 16:34). Now prophets of Yahweh live there (verse 5), and Elisha will heal its water (verses 19-22).

records.source: וַיִּגְּשׁ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־בִּֽירִיחוֹ֮ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הֲיָדַ֕עְתָּ כִּ֣י הַיּ֗וֹם יְהוָ֛ה לֹקֵ֥חַ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ מֵעַ֣ל רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם־אֲנִ֥י יָדַ֖עְתִּי הֶחֱשֽׁוּ׃
records.gloss: And drew near [the] sons of the prophets who [were] at Jericho to Elisha and said to him, Do you know that today Yahweh [is] taking your master from over your head? And he said, Also I know; be silent.
pieces: The company of prophets who were at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master from you today?" He answered, "Yes, I know. Say no more."

L.5: And the sons of the prophets who [were] at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is taking your master from over your head?" And he said, "I also know [it]; be silent."

R.5: The group of prophets at Jericho came up to Elisha and asked him, "Do you know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to take your master away from you today?" "Yes, I know," he answered. "Do not talk about it."

decisions.choice: the same question and answer as at Bethel
decisions.reason: The prophets at Jericho repeat the words of those at Bethel (verse 3), and Elisha answers the same way. The repetition slows the story as the moment comes near.

decisions.choice: company of prophets / group of prophets
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ שֵֽׁב־נָ֣א פֹ֗ה כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי הַיַּרְדֵּ֔נָה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said to him Elijah, Stay please here, for Yahweh has sent me to the Jordan; and he said, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I will leave you; and went the two of them.
pieces: Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." And the two of them walked on.

L.6: And Elijah said to him, "Stay here, please, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to the Jordan." And he said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." And the two of them went on.

R.6: Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to the Jordan River." But Elisha answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them kept walking together.

decisions.choice: the oath a third time
decisions.reason: As in verse 2. The third refusal shows that Elisha will not be turned back.

decisions.choice: the Jordan: the river east of Jericho
decisions.reason: Elijah came from Gilead, east of the Jordan (1 Kings 17:1). His journey leads him back across the river, toward the region where Moses was taken from Israel (Deuteronomy 34:1-6).

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" so the reader knows what the Jordan is.

records.source: וַחֲמִשִּׁ֨ים אִ֜ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֤י הַנְּבִיאִים֙ הָֽלְכ֔וּ וַיַּעַמְד֥וּ מִנֶּ֖גֶד מֵרָח֑וֹק וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם עָמְד֥וּ עַל־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And fifty men from [the] sons of the prophets went and stood opposite at a distance; and the two of them stood by the Jordan.
pieces: Fifty men of the company of prophets went along and stood some distance away, facing them, while the two of them stood beside the Jordan.

L.7: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite [them] at a distance, and the two of them stood by the Jordan.

R.7: Fifty men from the group of prophets also went. They stood a long way off and watched, while Elijah and Elisha stood beside the Jordan.

decisions.choice: stood opposite at a distance: they watched from far off
decisions.reason: The prophets keep their distance but stand where they can see. They are witnesses of what happens at the river (verse 15).

decisions.choice: watched; Elijah and Elisha
decisions.reason: Readable says that the men watched, which standing "opposite" implies, and names the two men for clarity.

records.source: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ אֶת־אַדַּרְתּ֤וֹ וַיִּגְלֹם֙ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם וַיֵּחָצ֖וּ הֵ֣נָּה וָהֵ֑נָּה וַיַּעַבְר֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בֶּחָרָבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And took Elijah his cloak and rolled [it] up and struck the waters, and they were divided here and here, and crossed the two of them on dry ground.
pieces: Then Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water. The water divided to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

L.8: And Elijah took his cloak and rolled [it] up and struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that way, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

R.8: Then Elijah took off his cloak, rolled it up and hit the water with it. The water split apart, part to one side and part to the other. And the two of them walked across on dry ground.

decisions.choice: the waters divided and they crossed on dry ground: as at the sea and at the Jordan before
decisions.reason: The words recall Moses stretching out his staff over the sea so that Israel crossed on dry ground (Exodus 14:16, 21-22), and the Jordan stopping for Israel under Joshua (Joshua 3:13-17), where the same word for dry ground is used. Elijah's cloak does what Moses' staff did, and the Jordan crossing is made again, this time in the other direction.

decisions.choice: his cloak: the prophet's outer garment, the mark of his office
decisions.reason: Elijah threw this cloak over Elisha when he called him (1 Kings 19:19), and wrapped his face in it on Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:13). Elisha will take it up (verse 13).

decisions.choice: rolled it up: folded or wrapped it together
decisions.reason: This verb is found only here. It seems to mean that Elijah rolled the cloak into a bundle, like a rod, to strike the water.

decisions.choice: this way and that way / to one side and the other
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "hither and hither"; the water stood on both sides of the path.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י כְעָבְרָ֗ם וְאֵ֨לִיָּ֜הוּ אָמַ֤ר אֶל־אֱלִישָׁע֙ שְׁאַל֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ בְּטֶ֖רֶם אֶלָּקַ֣ח מֵעִמָּ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע וִֽיהִי־נָ֛א פִּֽי־שְׁנַ֥יִם בְּרוּחֲךָ֖ אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And it was, as they crossed, and Elijah said to Elisha, Ask what I may do for you before I am taken from with you; and said Elisha, And let be please a mouth of two in your spirit to me.
pieces: When they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, "Before I am taken from you, tell me what I can do for you." Elisha answered, "Please let me receive a double portion of your spirit."

L.9: And it came about, as they crossed, that Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you." And Elisha said, "Please let there be a double portion of your spirit for me."

R.9: After they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "I am about to be taken away from you. Before that happens, what can I do for you? Ask me." Elisha answered, "Please give me a double share of your spirit, the share that goes to a firstborn son."

decisions.choice: a mouth of two: a double portion, the share of the firstborn heir
alternatives: twice as much of your spirit as you have
decisions.reason: "A mouth of two" is the phrase the law uses for the firstborn son's inheritance: he receives a double share of what his father leaves (Deuteronomy 21:17). Elisha is not asking to be twice as great as Elijah. He asks to be Elijah's chief heir and successor, the son who carries on his father's work (verse 12). In Zechariah 13:8 the same phrase means two parts out of three, which also fits the idea of the larger share.

decisions.choice: your spirit: the power of God at work in Elijah as a prophet
decisions.reason: Elijah's spirit is the prophetic power with which Yahweh filled him. The prophets later see that this spirit now rests on Elisha (verse 15), as Yahweh once put the spirit that was on Moses on the elders (Numbers 11:17, 25).

decisions.choice: you: Elisha, in a less common spelling
decisions.reason: The word for "you" is written here and in verse 10 in a form that usually speaks to a woman. It is an older or local way of writing the word for a man, and it still means Elisha.

decisions.choice: the share that goes to a firstborn son
decisions.reason: Readable explains the double portion, as m1 does, so that the reader does not take it to mean twice Elijah's power.

decisions.choice: I am about to be taken away from you. Before that happens, what can I do for you?
decisions.reason: Readable splits Elijah's request into short sentences.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִקְשִׁ֣יתָ לִשְׁא֑וֹל אִם־תִּרְאֶ֨ה אֹתִ֜י לֻקָּ֤ח מֵֽאִתָּךְ֙ יְהִֽי־לְךָ֣ כֵ֔ן וְאִם־אַ֖יִן לֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said, You have made hard to ask; if you see me taken from with you, let it be to you so; and if not, it will not be.
pieces: Elijah said, "You have asked for something difficult. If you see me being taken from you, you will have it; if you do not, you will not."

L.10: And he said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it will not be [so]."

R.10: Elijah said, "You have asked for something hard to give. But if you see me when I am taken away from you, you will have it. If you do not see me, you will not have it."

decisions.choice: you have made it hard to ask: what you ask is difficult
decisions.reason: Elijah cannot simply give his spirit; it is Yahweh's to give. He sets a sign by which Elisha will know whether Yahweh has granted it.

decisions.choice: if you see me taken: seeing is the sign that the request is granted
decisions.reason: To see Elijah taken up is to be allowed to see what is hidden from others, as Elisha's servant later sees the fiery horses and chariots around them (6:17). If Yahweh opens Elisha's eyes to it, he has also given him Elijah's spirit.

decisions.choice: Elijah said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י הֵ֣מָּה הֹלְכִ֤ים הָלוֹךְ֙ וְדַבֵּ֔ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה רֶֽכֶב־אֵשׁ֙ וְס֣וּסֵי אֵ֔שׁ וַיַּפְרִ֖דוּ בֵּ֣ין שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּ֨עַל֙ אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּֽסְעָרָ֖ה הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it was, they [were] walking, walking and speaking, and look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and they separated between the two of them; and went up Elijah in the whirlwind [to] the heavens.
pieces: As they were walking along and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire with horses of fire came between the two of them, and Elijah went up to heaven in the whirlwind.

L.11: And it came about, as they were walking on and speaking, that look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire [came], and they separated the two of them; and Elijah went up in the whirlwind [to] the heavens.

R.11: They were still walking along and talking. Then suddenly a chariot of fire pulled by horses of fire came between them and separated them. And Elijah went up into heaven in the whirlwind.

decisions.choice: walking, walking and speaking: they went on talking as they walked
decisions.reason: The repeated verb shows that they kept on walking and talking. The last thing the two do together is talk.

decisions.choice: chariot of fire and horses of fire: Yahweh's heavenly army
decisions.reason: Fire often shows Yahweh's presence (Exodus 3:2; 19:18). Chariots and horses were the strongest force of an army; these of fire belong to Yahweh's own host, as the horses and chariots of fire around Elisha do later (6:17).

decisions.choice: Elijah went up in the whirlwind: the chariot separates them, the wind takes him up
decisions.reason: The chariot and horses come between the two men; the text says that Elijah went up "in the whirlwind", as verse 1 said. It does not say that he rode in the chariot.

decisions.choice: Elijah went up to heaven: he did not die
decisions.reason: Elijah is taken alive, as Enoch was taken by God (Genesis 5:24). Unlike Moses, whose death and burial are told (Deuteronomy 34:5-6), Elijah has no grave. Malachi 3:23 later promises that he will be sent again before the day of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: [came] / came between
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the sight before the reader with "look" and then says that the horses separated the two; English needs a verb of coming.

records.source: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֣ע רֹאֶ֗ה וְה֤וּא מְצַעֵק֙ אָבִ֣י׀אָבִ֗י רֶ֤כֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפָ֣רָשָׁ֔יו וְלֹ֥א רָאָ֖הוּ ע֑וֹד וַֽיַּחֲזֵק֙ בִּבְגָדָ֔יו וַיִּקְרָעֵ֖ם לִשְׁנַ֥יִם קְרָעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Elisha [was] seeing, and he [was] crying out, My father, my father, [the] chariotry of Israel and its horsemen! And not he saw him again; and he took hold of his clothes and tore them into two pieces.
pieces: Elisha saw it, and he cried out, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" And he did not see him again. Then he gripped his own garments and tore them in two.

L.12: And Elisha saw [it], and he was crying out, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" And he did not see him again. And he took hold of his own clothes and tore them into two pieces.

R.12: Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father! Israel's chariots and horsemen!" Then Elisha could not see Elijah any longer. He grabbed his own clothes and ripped them in two.

decisions.choice: my father: a title of honor for the prophet who led him
decisions.reason: Elisha calls his master "father" as a disciple honors his teacher; the members of a company of prophets were called its "sons" (verse 3). The cry is also one of grief at a father's loss, and Elisha is the son who inherits (verse 9).

decisions.choice: the chariots of Israel and its horsemen: Elijah was Israel's true defense
alternatives: Elisha names the fiery chariot and horses he is watching
decisions.reason: Chariots and horsemen were a kingdom's strength in war. Elisha's cry most likely means that Elijah, through whom Yahweh worked, did more to protect Israel than all its chariots. King Joash says the same words over the dying Elisha (13:14). It is also possible that Elisha is naming the fiery chariot and horses he sees (verse 11) as Israel's real army, Yahweh's own.

decisions.choice: tore his clothes in two: mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the usual sign of grief at a death (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 1:11). Elisha mourns, and then takes up Elijah's cloak in place of his own torn garment (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the chariots
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is singular but means chariots as a force, as in 1 Kings 9:22.

decisions.choice: could not see Elijah
decisions.reason: Readable names Elijah where the Hebrew has "him".

records.source: וַיָּ֨רֶם֙ אֶת־אַדֶּ֣רֶת אֵלִיָּ֔הוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָפְלָ֖ה מֵעָלָ֑יו וַיָּ֥שָׁב וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And he picked up the cloak of Elijah which had fallen from on him, and went back and stood on [the] bank of the Jordan.
pieces: He picked up Elijah's cloak, which had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

L.13: And he picked up the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him, and he went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

R.13: Then Elisha picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah. He went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: the cloak that had fallen from him: Elijah's office passes to Elisha
decisions.reason: When Elijah called Elisha he threw this cloak over him (1 Kings 19:19). Now it has fallen from Elijah, and Elisha takes it up as the one who inherits his place.

decisions.choice: Elisha; the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable names Elisha and adds "River" for clarity.

records.source: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֶת־אַדֶּ֨רֶת אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֲשֶׁר־נָפְלָ֤ה מֵֽעָלָיו֙ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אַיֵּ֕ה יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ אַף־ה֣וּא׀וַיַּכֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַמַּ֗יִם וַיֵּֽחָצוּ֙ הֵ֣נָּה וָהֵ֔נָּה וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר אֱלִישָֽׁע׃
records.gloss: And he took the cloak of Elijah which had fallen from on him, and struck the waters and said, Where [is] Yahweh, [the] God of Elijah? Also he, and he struck the waters, and they were divided here and here; and crossed Elisha.
pieces: He took Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him, struck the water and said, "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Elijah?" When he too had struck the water, it divided to one side and the other, and Elisha crossed over.

L.14: And he took the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters, and said, "Where [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Elijah?" He also, when he had struck the waters, they were divided this way and that way, and Elisha crossed over.

R.14: He took the cloak that had fallen from Elijah and hit the water with it. "Where is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Elijah?" he asked. When Elisha also had struck the water, it split apart, part to one side and part to the other. And Elisha walked across.

decisions.choice: Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah?: a call on Yahweh to act now as he acted for Elijah
decisions.reason: Elisha is not doubting. He calls on Elijah's God to show that he is with Elisha too, and the waters divide as they did for Elijah (verse 8). It is the first sign that Elijah's spirit is on him (verse 15).

decisions.choice: "he also" begins the next clause: when he too struck the water
alternatives: Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah, even he?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew accents end Elisha's question at "the God of Elijah" and join "he also" to what follows: Elisha also, like Elijah before him, struck the water. The words could instead end the question: "Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah, even he?"

decisions.choice: struck the water twice: one action told twice
alternatives: the water did not part at the first stroke
decisions.reason: The verse first tells that Elisha struck the water and spoke, then repeats "he struck the water" to tell what followed. It most likely means one striking, not a first that failed and a second that worked.

decisions.choice: divided this way and that, and Elisha crossed: as Joshua followed Moses
decisions.reason: Elisha repeats Elijah's miracle (verse 8), as Joshua led Israel through the Jordan after Moses had led them through the sea (Joshua 3:7; 4:14, 23). Elisha comes back into the land by the way Israel first entered it.

records.source: וַיִּרְאֻ֨הוּ בְנֵֽי־הַנְּבִיאִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־בִּֽירִיחוֹ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ נָ֛חָה ר֥וּחַ אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ עַל־אֱלִישָׁ֑ע וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֖וֹ אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And saw him [the] sons of the prophets who [were] at Jericho from opposite, and they said, Has rested [the] spirit of Elijah on Elisha; and they came to meet him and bowed down to him to [the] ground.
pieces: When the company of prophets from Jericho, who were watching from the other side, saw him, they said, "The spirit of Elijah has come to rest on Elisha." They went to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

L.15: And the sons of the prophets who [were] at Jericho saw him from opposite, and they said, "The spirit of Elijah has come to rest on Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.

R.15: The group of prophets from Jericho had been watching from a distance. When they saw what Elisha did, they said, "The spirit of Elijah is now on Elisha." They went to meet him, and they bowed down to the ground in front of him.

decisions.choice: the spirit of Elijah has rested on Elisha: Elijah's prophetic power now works in Elisha
decisions.reason: The prophets see the sign at the river and know that Elisha has received what he asked for (verses 9-10). The spirit is Elijah's in the sense that it worked through him; it comes from Yahweh (verse 16; Numbers 11:25).

decisions.choice: bowed down to the ground: they accept Elisha as their leader
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was a sign of deep respect, given to a king or a master. The prophets now honor Elisha as they did Elijah.

decisions.choice: from opposite: from where they stood watching across the river
decisions.reason: The fifty prophets had stood at a distance facing the river (verse 7). They saw Elisha come back across it.

decisions.choice: saw what Elisha did
decisions.reason: Readable says what they saw: the water parting at Elisha's stroke, which is why they speak of Elijah's spirit.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֡יו הִנֵּה־נָ֣א יֵֽשׁ־אֶת־עֲבָדֶיךָ֩ חֲמִשִּׁ֨ים אֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּנֵֽי־חַ֗יִל יֵ֣לְכוּ נָא֮ וִיבַקְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־אֲדֹנֶיךָ֒ פֶּן־נְשָׂאוֹ֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלִכֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הֶהָרִ֔ים א֖וֹ בְּאַחַ֣ת הַגֵּאָי֑וֹת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֥א תִשְׁלָֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: And they said to him, Look please, there are with your servants fifty men, sons of strength; let them go please and search for your master, lest has carried him [the] Spirit of Yahweh and has thrown him on one of the mountains or into one of the valleys; and he said, Not you shall send.
pieces: They said to him, "Look, we your servants have fifty strong men with us. Please let them go and look for your master. It may be that the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has carried him off and set him down on some mountain or in some valley." But he said, "Do not send them."

L.16: And they said to him, "Look, please, there are with your servants fifty men, sons of strength. Let them go, please, and search for your master, in case the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has carried him off and thrown him on one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." And he said, "You shall not send [them]."

R.16: They said to Elisha, "Look, we your servants have fifty strong men here. Please let them go and look for your master. Maybe the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has picked him up and dropped him on some mountain or in some valley." But Elisha said, "No, do not send them."

decisions.choice: your servants: a polite way of saying "we"
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as the other person's servant was a courteous way to address a superior (1 Samuel 25:41). The prophets now speak to Elisha as their master.

decisions.choice: sons of strength: capable, strong men
decisions.reason: "Sons of strength" means men of ability and vigor, fit for a hard search in the hills.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Yahweh may have carried him off: a fear raised before about Elijah
decisions.reason: Obadiah once feared that the Spirit of Yahweh would carry Elijah away to some unknown place (1 Kings 18:12). The prophets think Elijah may have been set down somewhere on earth; Elisha, who saw him taken up, knows he will not be found.

decisions.choice: we your servants
decisions.reason: "Your servant" is kept at every level, as in Genesis 18:3 and 1 Samuel 20. Balanced and Readable add "we" so it is clear that the speakers mean themselves.

decisions.choice: set him down / dropped him
decisions.reason: The verb "threw" means that the Spirit put him down in some place; Balanced and Readable avoid the picture of a violent throw.

records.source: וַיִּפְצְרוּ־ב֥וֹ עַד־בֹּ֖שׁ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלָ֑חוּ וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ וַיְבַקְשׁ֥וּ שְׁלֹשָֽׁה־יָמִ֖ים וְלֹ֥א מְצָאֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And they urged him until being ashamed, and he said, Send; and they sent fifty men, and they searched three days and not found him.
pieces: But they kept pressing him until he was embarrassed to refuse, so he said, "Send them." They sent fifty men, and for three days they searched but did not find him.

L.17: And they pressed him until [he was] ashamed, and he said, "Send [them]." And they sent fifty men, and they searched three days but did not find him.

R.17: But they kept on begging him until he was too embarrassed to say no. So he said, "All right, send them." They sent fifty men, who looked for Elijah for three days. But they did not find him.

decisions.choice: until he was ashamed: until he could no longer refuse
decisions.reason: Elisha gives way not because he has changed his mind but because refusing again would be shameful in the face of their pleading (compare Judges 3:25).

decisions.choice: embarrassed to refuse / too embarrassed to say no
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the shame was about.

decisions.choice: looked for Elijah
decisions.reason: Readable names Elijah where the Hebrew has "him".

records.source: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ אֵלָ֔יו וְה֖וּא יֹשֵׁ֣ב בִּירִיח֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם הֲלֽוֹא־אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אַל־תֵּלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: And they returned to him, and he [was] staying at Jericho; and he said to them, Did I not say to you, Do not go?
pieces: When they came back to him, he was staying at Jericho. He said to them, "Did I not tell you not to go?"

L.18: And they returned to him, and he [was] staying at Jericho. And he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not go'?"

R.18: When they came back to Elisha, he was still at Jericho. He said to them, "I told you not to go, did I not?"

decisions.choice: Did I not say to you: a question that means "I told you so"
decisions.reason: Elisha's question expects the answer yes. His word has proved true, which shows him to be a true prophet.

decisions.choice: I told you not to go, did I not?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the question a statement with a short question at the end, which keeps its point clear.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֔ע הִנֵּה־נָ֞א מוֹשַׁ֤ב הָעִיר֙ ט֔וֹב כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י רֹאֶ֑ה וְהַמַּ֥יִם רָעִ֖ים וְהָאָ֥רֶץ מְשַׁכָּֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: And said the men of the city to Elisha, Look please, the location of the city [is] good, as my lord [is] seeing, but the waters [are] bad and the land [is] causing miscarriage.
pieces: The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, my lord, as you can see, this city is in a good place, but the water is bad, and the land causes miscarriages."

L.19: And the men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, please, the location of the city [is] good, as my lord sees, but the water [is] bad, and the land causes miscarriage."

R.19: The men of Jericho said to Elisha, "Sir, you can see that our town is in a fine place. But the water is bad, and nothing in the land bears young or fruit as it should."

decisions.choice: causing miscarriage: the land makes living things lose their young
decisions.reason: The word describes a mother losing her young before birth or a tree dropping its fruit (Exodus 23:26; Malachi 3:11). The bad water seems to have caused miscarriages among people and animals and perhaps poor harvests too. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: bad water at Jericho: the city once under Joshua's curse
decisions.reason: Joshua cursed the man who would rebuild Jericho with the loss of his firstborn and youngest sons (Joshua 6:26; 1 Kings 16:34). The loss of young in the land may recall that curse, which Yahweh now lifts (verse 21).

decisions.choice: my lord: polite address to Elisha
decisions.reason: The men address the prophet with respect, as people did a superior.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain polite form of address.

decisions.choice: nothing in the land bears young or fruit as it should
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the effect in general terms, as m1 explains.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קְחוּ־לִי֙ צְלֹחִ֣ית חֲדָשָׁ֔ה וְשִׂ֥ימוּ שָׁ֖ם מֶ֑לַח וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he said, Bring to me a new bowl and put there salt; and they brought [it] to him.
pieces: He said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.

L.20: And he said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." And they brought [it] to him.

R.20: Elisha said, "Bring me a new bowl with some salt in it." They brought it.

decisions.choice: a new bowl with salt: clean things for a holy act
decisions.reason: A new bowl had not been used for anything common, so it was fit for a sign of Yahweh's work. Salt was used with offerings (Leviticus 2:13) and stood for what lasts. Salt could also make land barren (Judges 9:45); here it is the sign of healing, but the healing is Yahweh's doing (verse 21).

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֙ אֶל־מוֹצָ֣א הַמַּ֔יִם וַיַּשְׁלֶךְ־שָׁ֖ם מֶ֑לַח וַיֹּ֜אמֶר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רִפִּ֨אתִי֙ לַמַּ֣יִם הָאֵ֔לֶּה לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה מִשָּׁ֛ם ע֖וֹד מָ֥וֶת וּמְשַׁכָּֽלֶת׃
records.gloss: And he went out to the source of the waters and threw there salt, and said, Thus says Yahweh, I have healed these waters; not will be from there again death and miscarriage.
pieces: Then he went out to the spring and threw the salt into it, and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'I have healed this water. From now on it will no longer cause death or miscarriage.'"

L.21: And he went out to the spring of the waters and threw salt there, and said, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'I have healed these waters; there will no longer be from there death or miscarriage.'"

R.21: Then Elisha went out to the spring where the water came from. He threw the salt in and announced, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'I have made this water healthy. It will never again cause death, or make the land lose its young.'"

decisions.choice: Thus says Yahweh, I have healed: the healing is Yahweh's, not the salt's
decisions.reason: Elisha speaks Yahweh's word. Yahweh, not the salt or the prophet, heals the water. The words recall Marah, where Yahweh made the bitter water sweet and called himself "Yahweh who heals you" (Exodus 15:25-26).

decisions.choice: the source of the waters: the spring that fed the city
decisions.reason: The word names the place where water comes out of the ground. A strong spring still flows at the site of ancient Jericho.

decisions.choice: miscarriage
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: made this water healthy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "healed" means for water: it is now safe and good.

records.source: וַיֵּרָפ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּדְבַ֥ר אֱלִישָׁ֖ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃פ
records.gloss: And were healed the waters until this day, according to [the] word of Elisha which he spoke.
pieces: So the water has been wholesome to this day, just as Elisha had said.

L.22: And the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.

R.22: And the water has stayed healthy to this day, just as Elisha said it would.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own time
decisions.reason: "To this day" means up to the time when this account was written. The writer points to something his readers could still see: Jericho's good water.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Elisha: Yahweh's word through his prophet comes true
decisions.reason: Elisha spoke in Yahweh's name (verse 21), and what he said happened. This marks him as a true prophet (Deuteronomy 18:22).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְה֣וּא׀עֹלֶ֣ה בַדֶּ֗רֶךְ וּנְעָרִ֤ים קְטַנִּים֙ יָצְא֣וּ מִן־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּתְקַלְּסוּ־בוֹ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ עֲלֵ֥ה קֵרֵ֖חַ עֲלֵ֥ה קֵרֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And he went up from there [to] Bethel; and he [was] going up on the way, and lads small came out from the city and jeered at him and said to him, Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!
pieces: From there Elisha went up to Bethel. As he was going up the road, some young lads came out of the city and mocked him, saying, "Go on up, baldhead! Go on up, baldhead!"

L.23: And he went up from there [to] Bethel. And as he was going up on the road, small lads came out from the city and jeered at him and said to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"

R.23: From Jericho, Elisha went up to Bethel. While he was walking up the road, some young lads came out of the town and made fun of him. They shouted, "Go on up, you bald head! Go on up, you bald head!"

decisions.choice: small lads: boys or young men, of an age not certain
decisions.reason: The word for "lads" covers anyone from a baby (Exodus 2:6) to a young man old enough to serve as a soldier or a servant (1 Samuel 17:33; 2 Samuel 2:14). "Small" may mean young in years, or simply young and of little account: King Solomon calls himself a "small lad" when he is already a grown man (1 Kings 3:7). A large band of them (verse 24) shouting at a prophet may suggest older youths rather than small children.

decisions.choice: Go up, baldhead!: an insult and a taunt
decisions.reason: Baldness was a mark of shame (Isaiah 3:24). Elisha may have been bald, or his head may have been shaved. "Go up" may mock Elijah's going up to heaven, as if to say "go away like your master", or it may simply mean "get away from here". Either way they scorn Yahweh's prophet.

decisions.choice: Bethel: the center of the calf worship
decisions.reason: Bethel was the royal shrine of the golden calf (1 Kings 12:28-29; Amos 7:13). The jeering comes from the city that had turned away from Yahweh's worship.

decisions.choice: young lads
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "young lads", which, like the Hebrew, leaves the age open between children and youths (m1).

decisions.choice: From Jericho
decisions.reason: Readable names the place Elisha left.

records.heading: Elisha at Bethel

records.source: וַיִּ֤פֶן אַֽחֲרָיו֙ וַיִּרְאֵ֔ם וַֽיְקַלְלֵ֖ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה שְׁתַּ֤יִם דֻּבִּים֙ מִן־הַיַּ֔עַר וַתְּבַקַּ֣עְנָה מֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וּשְׁנֵ֖י יְלָדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he turned behind him and saw them and cursed them in [the] name of Yahweh; and came out two she-bears from the forest and tore of them forty-two children.
pieces: He turned around, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then two female bears came out of the forest and savaged forty-two of the youngsters.

L.24: And he turned around and saw them, and he cursed them in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And two she-bears came out of the forest and tore forty-two of the children.

R.24: Elisha turned around and looked at them. He put a curse on them in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then two mother bears came out of the woods and attacked them. They tore up forty-two of the young people.

decisions.choice: cursed them in the name of Yahweh: he called on Yahweh to judge them
decisions.reason: Elisha does not act by his own power. He calls on Yahweh, and what happens is Yahweh's response. To scorn Yahweh's prophet was to scorn Yahweh (compare 1:9-12). Wild animals were among the punishments the covenant warned of for a people that turned from Yahweh; Leviticus 26:22 says they would rob Israel of its children, using the verb behind "miscarriage" in verse 19.

decisions.choice: she-bears: female bears
decisions.reason: The verb that follows is feminine, so the bears are females, perhaps mothers with cubs, who are the most dangerous (2 Samuel 17:8).

decisions.choice: tore: wounded, without saying whether they died
decisions.reason: The verb means to rip or tear open. The text does not say whether all forty-two died.

decisions.choice: children: young people
decisions.reason: This word is used for children and also for young men (1 Kings 12:8, where Rehoboam's companions are called by it). It leaves their age as open as "lads" in verse 23.

decisions.choice: youngsters / young people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose words that, like the Hebrew, leave the age open (m4).

decisions.choice: mother bears
decisions.reason: Readable takes up the hint that the bears were mothers (m2); a female bear with cubs is the danger 2 Samuel 17:8 speaks of.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶל־הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וּמִשָּׁ֖ם שָׁ֥ב שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: And he went from there to Mount the Carmel, and from there he returned [to] Samaria.
pieces: From there he went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he went back to Samaria.

L.25: And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned [to] Samaria.

R.25: From Bethel, Elisha went on to Mount Carmel. Then he went back to the city of Samaria.

decisions.choice: Mount Carmel: where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal
decisions.reason: Carmel was the place of Elijah's great contest with the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18:19-40). Elisha later lived there for a time (4:25).

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria was the royal city built by Omri (1 Kings 16:24). Elisha's work will often bring him before Israel's kings there.

decisions.choice: From Bethel; the city of Samaria
decisions.reason: Readable names the place he left and makes clear that Samaria is a city.
